FAYUVI, also known as UX111, is a single-dose AAV9 gene therapy designed for children with mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIA (MPS IIIA). It is an ultra-rare and fatal lysosomal storage disease that causes progressive neurodegeneration, with a median life expectancy of 15 years.

The approval marks Ultragenyx’s second gene therapy success and includes a Priority Review Voucher. The FDA incentive can be used to speed up the review of a future drug or sold to another drugmaker. Past vouchers have sold for hundreds of millions of dollars.

children: , chief executive officer and president of Ultragenyx, said the approval reflects “years of research from scientists and developers” and support from patient families, calling it a “historic milestone” for a community that had waited for a treatment option.

The approval rests on data from the pivotal Transpher A trial and long-term follow-up, with clinical data now extending to nearly eight years. FAYUVI-treated patients (mITT population, N=17) showed a 23.5-point higher Bayley-III cognitive score (p<0.0001) than an external, untreated natural-history cohort (N=27).

FAYUVI is manufactured entirely in the U.S., at facilities in Bedford, Massachusetts and Columbus, Ohio. Ultragenyx expects the commercial product to reach Qualified Treatment Centers within 30 to 60 days.
